name: Barbell Row
description: The barbell row is a horizontal pulling exercise performed in a hinged position with a barbell. It trains the latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and middle trapezius as primary movers and places significant isometric demand on the erector spinae and hamstrings to maintain the hip-hinge position. It is one of the most effective exercises for overall back thickness and strength.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart over the barbell. Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, with a slight knee bend. Grip the bar just outside shoulder width with an overhand or underhand grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Set up like the start of a deadlift but with a more pronounced hip hinge to get the torso near-parallel to the floor. Maintain a neutral spine. Brace the core and engage the lats before each rep.
steps: With a neutral spine and braced core, row the barbell toward your lower rib cage.
Lead with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar under control back toward the floor, maintaining the hinge position throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you row the bar up. Inhale as you lower it.
common_mistakes: Allowing the lower back to round under load
Using body English and hip drive to jerk the bar up instead of pulling with the back
Pulling the bar to the waist rather than the lower ribs, reducing lat involvement
safety_considerations: Never compromise spinal position for more weight
If unable to maintain a hip-hinge position, reduce load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension of the arms at the bottom, bar touches or nearly touches the lower ribs at the top.
coaching_cues: Row the bar into your hip pockets
Keep your chest up and your spine long throughout every rep
